lines.text: Tomorrow night, the horde reaches the fence. Tonight was our last quiet one. Oakhaven. Day twenty. The surplus store won. Six votes. Ryan went in alone, and it was quiet. Too quiet, for too long. He was halfway through the stockroom when the dead started showing up at the front windows. A few. Then a dozen. Then more, drawn in by the noise. He grabbed what he could carry and went out the back. Food, water, and medicine. But he had to leave a whole rack of military gear behind. Plate carrier vests, helmets, and ammo pouches, some still in the plastic. Ryan is going back for the rest. Steve is back on his feet, sling and all. Tanny has been watching Elias since the rain, and trying hard not to look like it. Behind the woodpile. Flat on the laundromat roof. Pretending to doze on the next cot over. At supper, Gabe, one of our medics, finally sat down and checked on him. A slight fever. A rattle in his chest. A pulse running a little fast. Elias rolled up both sleeves without being asked, and let Gabe look all he wanted. "Chest cold, friend. Too many nights on that roof." He took the aspirin, thanked Gabe twice, and asked him when his birthday was. Tanny says Elias slept sitting up again, back to the wall. And this morning, walking past the woodpile, Elias said, "Morning, Tanny," without ever looking up. Forty-three of us. Food for one more day. Water for two. And tomorrow night, they hit the fence. Where do we go before they get here? The arcade, never searched. The show barn, nobody knows what's inside. Or the harvest, the corn and wheat, before the frost. Comment your name and your job, to move in.
